methodology: Agent metadata audit: screen every category changed by the merged commit, plus a deterministic hash-selected sample of 30 unchanged NLP assignments excluding all three development fixture files. Inspect titles and stored publisher descriptions; inspect field metadata and re-fetch public layer definitions for 19 targeted questionable records. No publisher rows were queried. Same agent that developed the rules performed this unblinded audit; this is not independent human ground truth.
limits: The merged commit includes 147 category changes, not only the final 40 discussed in chat. 145 were previously Uncategorized; two were already categorized.
Changed records include development examples and repeated layers, so agreement cannot be interpreted as held-out accuracy.
The separate 30-record sample excludes development fixtures and changed records, but is small, may contain related services, and cannot establish catalog-wide accuracy.
Likely mismatches are reviewer judgments based on dataset purpose; ambiguous cases require an explicit taxonomy policy.
Uncategorized records, curated entries and recall were not assessed; data correctness and endpoint availability were not scored.

rows.title: Central Tampa Planning District (R-10, R-20, R-35 Parcels)
rows.reason: The service computes parcel residential capacity from future land use. Planning, Housing and Development all apply; a title-only winner does not prove the best primary category.

evidence.description: Residential Capacity Utilization Methodology Maximum Allowed Units are estimated by multiplying a parcel’s gross acreage by the maximum residential density indicated by its Future Land Use (FLU) category (e.g., R-10 = 10 units per acre, R-20 = 20 units per acre, and R-35 = 35 units per acre). Fractional results are rounded down to the nearest whole unit, with a minimum of one unit for parcels with a positive calculated capacity below one unit. Capacity Utilization (%) is calculated by dividing the actual number of residential units by the estimated maximum allowed units and multiplying by 100. Aggregated Bin Utilization (%) is calculated by dividing the sum of actual residential units by the sum of estimated maximum allowed units within each bin and multiplying by 100. These estimates are based on FLU density and parcel acreage. Actual development potential may differ due to zoning regulations, density bonuses, exceptions, and other applicable development standards.

evidence.description: ClearCast City of St. Petersburg coastal guidance. Observed window: previous 24 hours; forecast model horizon: 120 hours. STOFS2D daily baseline; valid local P-Surge enables e50 most-likely and e10 high-end coastal guidance with WPC P90 rainfall. Source cycle/advisory is recorded in latest-run metadata. Coastal inundation is derived by interpolating selected coastal forecast reference levels over terrain; rainfall is a separate guidance overlay, not a coupled rainfall/runoff simulation. Latest operational records replace previous records; event archives are maintained in Clearview Azure.
